tables.description: Flight departures, one row per flight date and flight number. Carrier, airport and aircraft attributes live in the dimensions -- a question about alliance, region or aircraft type requires a join. KNOWN DEFECTS: arrival_delay_minutes is NULL on about 1.5% of operated flights the feed did not report, and a handful of rows carry a 2019 flight_date outside the 2023-2024 period this warehouse covers.

columns.name: flight_date
columns.description: Date of the scheduled departure. The warehouse covers 2023-01-01 to 2024-12-31; a few feed-error rows fall outside it and have no dim_date row, so an unbounded aggregate disagrees with one joined to the calendar.

columns.name: flight_number
columns.description: Carrier-prefixed flight number, unique within a date

columns.name: carrier_code
columns.description: Operating carrier; joins to dim_carrier.carrier_code

columns.name: tail_number
columns.description: Airframe operating the flight; joins to dim_aircraft.tail_number

columns.name: origin_airport
columns.description: Departure airport; joins to dim_airport.airport_code

columns.name: destination_airport
columns.description: Arrival airport; joins to dim_airport.airport_code

columns.name: distance_km
columns.description: Great-circle route distance in kilometres. A property of the route, identical on every flight of it.

columns.name: seats
columns.description: Seats offered for sale on this departure. Not the airframe's capacity -- that is dim_aircraft.seat_capacity.

columns.name: passengers
columns.description: Passengers who boarded

columns.name: fare_eur
columns.description: Average fare paid per passenger on this departure, in EUR. A rate, not a total: do not SUM it.

columns.name: departure_delay_minutes
columns.description: Minutes late leaving the gate; negative means early

columns.name: arrival_delay_minutes
columns.description: Minutes late at the arrival gate; negative means early. A flight is on time at 15 minutes or less.

columns.name: cancelled_flag
columns.description: 1 if the flight was cancelled, 0 otherwise. A cancelled flight carries no passengers and no delay.

tables.description: Fuel uplift, one row per fuel date and tail number -- NOT per flight. An airframe flies several times a day, so joining this to fact_flights on the tail and the date multiplies every flight row by that day's fuel record.

columns.name: fuel_date
columns.description: Date the fuel was uplifted

columns.name: tail_number
columns.description: Airframe fuelled; joins to dim_aircraft.tail_number

columns.name: fuel_litres
columns.description: Litres uplifted across the whole day for this airframe

columns.name: fuel_cost_eur
columns.description: Cost of that uplift in EUR

tables.description: Operating carriers, one row per carrier code.

columns.name: carrier_code
columns.description: Two-letter carrier code

columns.name: carrier_name
columns.description: Carrier's trading name

columns.name: alliance
columns.description: Alliance membership, or 'Unaligned' for a carrier in none

columns.name: service_model
columns.description: FullService, LowCost or Regional

tables.description: Airports, one row per airport code. Both the origin and the destination of a flight join here.

columns.name: airport_code
columns.description: Three-letter IATA-style airport code

columns.name: city
columns.description: City served

columns.name: country
columns.description: Country the airport is in

columns.name: region
columns.description: Geographic region grouping, e.g. Europe-West

columns.name: hub_size
columns.description: Congestion tier: mega_hub, large_hub, medium_hub or small_hub

tables.description: Airframes, one row per tail number and validity window -- a slowly-changing dimension, NOT a lookup. Two tails changed operator mid-period and therefore have two rows each, so joining on tail_number alone multiplies those tails' flights. Join on the validity window as well: ON f.tail_number = ac.tail_number AND f.flight_date >= ac.valid_from AND f.flight_date < ac.valid_to.

columns.name: tail_number
columns.description: Registration of the airframe

columns.name: carrier_code
columns.description: Carrier that operates this airframe

columns.name: aircraft_type
columns.description: Type designation, e.g. A320neo

columns.name: manufacturer
columns.description: Airbus, Boeing or Embraer

columns.name: body_type
columns.description: Narrowbody, Widebody or Regional

columns.name: seat_capacity
columns.description: Seats the airframe is configured for. Not the seats sold on a given flight -- that is fact_flights.seats.

columns.name: year_built
columns.description: Year the airframe entered service

columns.name: valid_from
columns.description: First date this row's attributes applied to the tail (inclusive).

columns.name: valid_to
columns.description: First date they no longer applied (exclusive); 9999-12-31 for the current row. Exclusive so the windows tile the period without overlapping -- a BETWEEN on them would match the changeover date twice.

tables.description: Calendar attributes, one row per flight date.

columns.name: flight_date
columns.description: The calendar date

columns.name: day_of_week
columns.description: Weekday name

columns.name: is_weekend
columns.description: 1 on Saturday and Sunday

columns.name: fiscal_quarter
columns.description: Quarter label, e.g. 2024-Q3

columns.name: season
columns.description: Winter, Spring, Summer or Autumn

columns.name: is_holiday
columns.description: 1 on a public holiday that moves traffic

tables.description: One row per crew member: who they fly for, what they fly as, and their contact details. The contact columns are personal data and are tagged as such in the governance block -- a caller without PII access sees them masked, and an expression computed over one is rejected rather than masked.

columns.name: crew_id
columns.description: Crew member identifier (primary key); pseudonymised for callers without PII access

columns.name: carrier_code
columns.description: Carrier the crew member flies for; joins to dim_carrier.carrier_code

columns.name: crew_name
columns.description: Crew member's full name. Personal data.

columns.name: crew_email
columns.description: Crew member's work email address. Personal data.

columns.name: crew_phone
columns.description: Crew member's contact number. Personal data.

columns.name: crew_role
columns.description: Captain, First Officer, Senior Cabin Crew or Cabin Crew

columns.name: base_airport
columns.description: Airport the crew member is based at

columns.name: hire_year
columns.description: Year the crew member joined the carrier

business_metrics.definition: SUM(CASE WHEN arrival_delay_minutes <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(arrival_delay_minutes)
business_metrics.description: Share of flights arriving within 15 minutes of schedule. Cancelled flights have no arrival and must be excluded with cancelled_flag = 0.
Passengers carried as a share of seats offered. Both legs are additive, so this is a ratio of sums, never an average of per-flight ratios.
Share of scheduled departures that did not operate.
Ticket revenue. fare_eur is a per-passenger rate, so it is multiplied by passengers, never summed on its own.
Mean arrival delay in minutes over operated flights. Distinct from on_time_rate: a carrier can have a good average and poor punctuality.

Litres per available seat-kilometre. Its two legs sit on tables at different grains -- fact_fuel is per tail-day, fact_flights per flight -- so it can only be computed by aggregating each side before joining.

missing_param_prompts.metric: metric (e.g. on-time rate, load factor, average delay)
missing_param_prompts.scope: network scope (e.g. carrier, route, airport, or aircraft type)

language.clarification_example: Example: "What was the on-time rate for LowCost carriers in 2024?"

topic_prompts.prompt:
Your disruption question needs more detail. Would you like to see:
• Punctuality — share of flights arriving within 15 minutes?
• Cancellations — share of departures that did not operate?
• Delay magnitude — average arrival delay in minutes?

Please re-state with: metric, timeframe, and network scope.

suggestions: What is the fuel cost per carrier in 2024?
Compare fuel litres by aircraft type.
What is the on-time rate by carrier?

Which service model has the highest cancellation rate?

default_recovery_ideas: What is the on-time rate by carrier?
Compare load factor by service model.

few_shot_examples.question: What is the on-time rate for each carrier in 2024?
few_shot_examples.sql:
SELECT c.carrier_name,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN f.arrival_delay_minutes <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0
             / COUNT(f.arrival_delay_minutes), 4) AS on_time_rate
FROM fact_flights AS f
JOIN dim_carrier AS c ON f.carrier_code = c.carrier_code
WHERE f.cancelled_flag = 0
  AND CAST(f.flight_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2024-01-01' AND DATE '2024-12-31'
GROUP BY c.carrier_name
ORDER BY on_time_rate DESC

few_shot_examples.question: Compare load factor across service models.
few_shot_examples.sql:
SELECT c.service_model,
       ROUND(SUM(f.passengers) * 1.0 / SUM(f.seats), 4) AS load_factor
FROM fact_flights AS f
JOIN dim_carrier AS c ON f.carrier_code = c.carrier_code
WHERE f.cancelled_flag = 0
GROUP BY c.service_model
ORDER BY load_factor DESC

few_shot_examples.question: Which origin region has the worst average arrival delay?
few_shot_examples.sql:
SELECT a.region,
       ROUND(AVG(f.arrival_delay_minutes), 2) AS avg_arrival_delay
FROM fact_flights AS f
JOIN dim_airport AS a ON f.origin_airport = a.airport_code
WHERE f.cancelled_flag = 0
GROUP BY a.region
ORDER BY avg_arrival_delay DESC

few_shot_examples.question: Show monthly passenger revenue.
few_shot_examples.sql:
SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', CAST(f.flight_date AS DATE)) AS month_start,
       ROUND(SUM(f.passengers * f.fare_eur), 2) AS passenger_revenue
FROM fact_flights AS f
WHERE f.cancelled_flag = 0
GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', CAST(f.flight_date AS DATE))
ORDER BY month_start

few_shot_examples.question: What is the cancellation rate by hub size of the origin airport?
few_shot_examples.sql:
SELECT a.hub_size,
       ROUND(SUM(f.cancelled_flag) * 1.0 / COUNT(*), 4) AS cancellation_rate
FROM fact_flights AS f
JOIN dim_airport AS a ON f.origin_airport = a.airport_code
GROUP BY a.hub_size
ORDER BY cancellation_rate DESC

few_shot_examples.question: Compare on-time rate month over month for 2024.
few_shot_examples.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', CAST(f.flight_date AS DATE)) AS month_start,
           SUM(CASE WHEN f.arrival_delay_minutes <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0
               / COUNT(f.arrival_delay_minutes) AS on_time_rate
    FROM fact_flights AS f
    WHERE f.cancelled_flag = 0
      AND CAST(f.flight_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2024-01-01' AND DATE '2024-12-31'
    GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', CAST(f.flight_date AS DATE))
)
SELECT month_start,
       ROUND(on_time_rate, 4) AS on_time_rate,
       ROUND(on_time_rate - LAG(on_time_rate) OVER (ORDER BY month_start), 4) AS delta
FROM monthly
ORDER BY month_start

few_shot_examples.question: What is fuel cost per seat-kilometre by aircraft type?
few_shot_examples.sql:
WITH flown AS (
    SELECT f.tail_number,
           SUM(f.seats * f.distance_km) AS seat_km
    FROM fact_flights AS f
    WHERE f.cancelled_flag = 0
    GROUP BY f.tail_number
), burned AS (
    SELECT u.tail_number,
           SUM(u.fuel_cost_eur) AS fuel_cost
    FROM fact_fuel AS u
    GROUP BY u.tail_number
)
SELECT ac.aircraft_type,
       ROUND(SUM(burned.fuel_cost) / NULLIF(SUM(flown.seat_km), 0), 6) AS fuel_cost_per_seat_km
FROM flown
JOIN burned ON flown.tail_number = burned.tail_number
JOIN dim_aircraft AS ac ON flown.tail_number = ac.tail_number
                       AND ac.valid_to = DATE '9999-12-31'
GROUP BY ac.aircraft_type
ORDER BY fuel_cost_per_seat_km

few_shot_examples.question: Which routes carried the most passengers in 2024?
few_shot_examples.sql:
SELECT o.city AS origin_city,
       d.city AS destination_city,
       SUM(f.passengers) AS passengers
FROM fact_flights AS f
JOIN dim_airport AS o ON f.origin_airport = o.airport_code
JOIN dim_airport AS d ON f.destination_airport = d.airport_code
WHERE f.cancelled_flag = 0
  AND CAST(f.flight_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2024-01-01' AND DATE '2024-12-31'
GROUP BY o.city, d.city
ORDER BY passengers DESC
LIMIT 10

few_shot_examples.question: Is the on-time rate worse on public holidays?
few_shot_examples.sql:
SELECT dd.is_holiday,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN f.arrival_delay_minutes <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0
             / COUNT(f.arrival_delay_minutes), 4) AS on_time_rate
FROM fact_flights AS f
JOIN dim_date AS dd ON f.flight_date = dd.flight_date
WHERE f.cancelled_flag = 0
GROUP BY dd.is_holiday
ORDER BY dd.is_holiday

few_shot_examples.question: Compare average arrival delay by alliance and season.
few_shot_examples.sql:
SELECT c.alliance,
       dd.season,
       ROUND(AVG(f.arrival_delay_minutes), 2) AS avg_arrival_delay
FROM fact_flights AS f
JOIN dim_carrier AS c ON f.carrier_code = c.carrier_code
JOIN dim_date AS dd ON f.flight_date = dd.flight_date
WHERE f.cancelled_flag = 0
GROUP BY c.alliance, dd.season
ORDER BY c.alliance, avg_arrival_delay DESC

row_policies.name: carrier_scope
row_policies.description: A carrier analyst reads only their own carrier's flights, airframes and crew. fact_fuel carries no carrier code, so it is scoped through the airframe that burned the fuel -- the restriction holds whether or not the query joined dim_aircraft. dim_aircraft is slowly-changing and two tails have transferred operator, so that semi-join is also closed on the validity window: without it both the old and the new operator read the whole of an airframe's fuel history.

pii.description: Identifies a person directly; there is no partial form of a name worth showing.
The domain is operationally useful and not identifying; the local part is the identity.
The last four digits are what a person uses to recognise their own number.
Not identifying on its own, but it is the join key to every other column here, so it is stably pseudonymised: a report can still group by crew member without naming one.
